John agreed!
The original brief

Grid batteries: why we stepped back

John's idea: a battery facility that buys cheap daytime power, sells it at evening peak prices, and later leases the storage to PSPCL.

Legal

Reselling power needs a CERC trading licence: Rs 5 crore net worth even at the smallest level.

Capital

One 600 MWh project in Gujarat cost about Rs 670 crore.

Competition

Large firms win state tenders on long contracts.

Time

Leasing to PSPCL pays only after the shift to renewables.

Expertise

Needs grid engineering and regulatory depth.

A good idea, but not one a small company or a student team could test.

Our counter proposal

Rooftop micro wind turbines

Why it fits

  • Needs a terrace corner, not the whole roof
  • Works at night and in the monsoon, when solar drops
  • Indian suppliers sell 1 kW units; some start at 1.5 m/s
  • Less cleaning than dusty solar panels
  • Almost empty market: only 3.35 MW of small wind in India
BESSRooftop wind
CapitalHundreds of croresRs 1 to 2 lakh a unit
LicenceCERC tradingNot for own use
Test now?NoYes, a pilot
ExpertiseGrid engineeringInstall and measure
MarketBig playersNiche, few players

How can Blue Jhasha bring small rooftop wind turbines to homes in the Chandigarh region as a low-space energy source that keeps working when solar stops?

How it works

From wind to your fan

1. Wind

pushes the blades, from any direction

2. Turbine

the spinning shaft drives a generator

3. Controller

steadies the power

4. Battery

stores it for later

5. Home

lights, fans, phones

Vertical axis

Catches wind from any direction, quieter, suits gusty city rooftops.

Mini 3 blade

Faces the wind, more efficient in steady wind such as the hills.

With a battery

Power is stored, so the home keeps using it when the wind drops.

Risks

What might not work, and the fix

LimitWhat we foundHow we will manage
Low wind in the plainsChandigarh averages only about 2 m/sPilot in hills and plains, judge on real data
Higher price than solar1 kW wind Rs 98,000 to 1.9 lakh; 1 kW solar Rs 60,000 to 80,000 (less with PM Surya Ghar)Sell on space and night power; EMI and a hybrid kit
Noise and vibrationHeld rooftop wind back beforeNewer vertical axis models; test noise on site
No subsidy todayMNRE small wind subsidy ended in 2017Build the case on payback
Short semesterSupplier replies and pilot data take timeContact suppliers early; document everything
Good news: Shimla stays above 2 m/s in every season

Indicators

How we'll know it worked

Pilot

  • Wind speed at each site (m/s)
  • Power made per day (kWh)
  • Hours of output at night

Business

  • Cost per unit vs solar
  • Payback period in years
  • Suppliers shortlisted

Visibility

  • Website and LinkedIn updated
  • Followers and views, before and after
  • John's feedback
